head: The Flames played last night
paras: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 7-3 in Calgary on Oct 8. The Flames (5-7-0) lost 4-0 to Edmonton on Wednesday, while the Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 the same night. The Flames played last night, and the Avalanche are rested. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 16th).

The Flames rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). Calgary has scored 2.33 goals a game, the third fewest in the league, and allowed 3.75, the second most. As for the Avalanche, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.15 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 12 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (4 G / 4 A / 8 P in 12 GP) has a team-high four goals. Nathan MacKinnon (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 13 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL, with a point in five straight games against Calgary. Artturi Lehkonen (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for third in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.

Dustin Wolf (1-4-0 / .839 SV% in 5 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start. Colorado has two options in net: Mackenzie Blackwood (6-3-0 / .894 SV% in 9 GS) and Scott Wedgewood (1-2-1 / .889 SV% in 4 GS). Blackwood has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Blackwood has a .939 save percentage in five starts against the Flames, well above his usual .905. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

items.text: The Flames are newly without Devin Cooley, have been without Samuel Honzek, Maxim Tsyplakov and Joel Hanley for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season. Dustin Wolf is expected to start.
Artturi Lehkonen has ten goals on chances worth about 4.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Mikael Backlund is one point from passing Johnny Gaudreau for fifth on the Flames’ all-time scoring list.
Zachary L'Heureux and Matt Coronato fought the last time these two met.

COL.head: A big edge for the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. It’s on the Flames to make it a game, and they can if they keep dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: The Avalanche should be favored
CGY.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Flames can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus Dustin Wolf stealing the show.

calls.head: The Flames played last night
calls.body: The Flames played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Avalanche to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: Blackwood’s hold on the Flames won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Blackwood has been a wall against the Flames, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Flames finally get to him.

calls.head: Expect the Avalanche to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Few teams shoot like the Avalanche, and the Flames are one of the league’s worst at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Flames’ end.

calls.head: Run and gun
calls.body: The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Avalanche. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
